title: Excess Flood Renewal Underwriting: Loss-History Surcharge on the Renewal Term Premium
content:
A renewal of an **Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines)** policy carries a loss-history surcharge read from recent claim payments on the home.

## Rule

The renewal loss-history adjustment counts claim payments issued fewer than 36 whole months before the renewal is booked: building payments on the claim file of the NFIP policy of the home or dwelling payments on the claim file of the HomeFlood policy of the home (primary payments), and claim payments on this excess policy (layer payments); each void of a claim payment posted in that same window takes one payment off the count. It is a surcharge of 25 percent where at least one layer payment or two or more primary payments stand, a surcharge of 10 percent where no layer payment and exactly one primary payment stands, and otherwise there is no loss-history adjustment.

The NFIP policy of the home is the Tidemark NFIP Dwelling Form policy (NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)) in force whose policy number is the underlying policy number on the excess policy record, and the HomeFlood policy of the home is the active Tidemark HomeFlood policy (HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies) whose policy number is that underlying policy number; of these two policies only their status, the NFIP policy's primary-residence designation, their claim payments and voided payments and the NFIP policy's applied Elevation Certificates are read. Where two entries on a file share the date they are read by, or two policy records answer the same description, the one entered first is read.

Every percentage selected for a renewal term is added into one net adjustment percentage, which acts once on the zone-factored layer charge after the elevation multiplier — that charge is multiplied by one plus the net adjustment percentage — and never on the loss-of-use charge.

## Combinations

| Layer payments standing | Primary payments standing | Loss-history adjustment |
|---|---|---|
| one or more | any number | surcharge of 25 percent |
| none | two or more | surcharge of 25 percent |
| none | exactly one | surcharge of 10 percent |
| none | none | none |

## The 36-month window

A payment counts when it was issued fewer than 36 whole months before the day the renewal is booked. For a renewal booked on the 15th of a month (hypothetical), a payment issued on the 16th of the same month three years earlier lies 35 whole months back and counts; one issued on the 15th lies 36 whole months back and does not. A void counts against the tally only when the void itself was posted inside the window.
